title: ℓ¹-Native Cohomology of Finite Defect Fields: Quotient Norms, Dual Circulations, Sparse Representatives, and the L^p Geometric Family
description:
Version: v6.5.2 (2026-10-15).

Abstract. For a finite directed graph or 2-simplicial complex equipped with strictly positive edge weights, we formulate and study the family of weighted Lp norms (p in [1, ∞), complemented by the separate weighted Chebyshev endpoint norm at p = ∞) induced on the first cochain quotient space Q1 = C1 / im(d0). Under this formulation, the quotient infimum is attained for all p in [1, ∞], defines a genuine quotient norm Φp on Q1, and satisfies Fenchel-Rockafellar strong duality pairing primal potential adjustments with dual divergence-free circulations. In the polyhedral base case p = 1, exact rational linear programming certifies sparse optimal representatives concentrated onto at most the cycle rank β. In the strictly convex regime p in (1, ∞), minimizers on gauge-fixed potentials solve the nonlinear graph p-Laplacian. On 2-complexes, coboundary nilpotency d1 d0 = 0 enforces discrete Bianchi identity conservation, while off-diagonal quantum state coherence is bounded under Schatten trace norms and additive real flux of a chosen real lift is distinguished from branch-independent U(1) phase holonomy and period-minimized quotient defect.

Artifacts. The deposit contains the complete research monograph in Markdown, XeLaTeX, and vector PDF; a verified Python computational engine operating under exact rational arithmetic for polyhedral and certificate decision paths (p = 1, 2, ∞) and binary64 solvers for continuous Lp and Schatten-p diagnostics with 110 test cases; Lean 4 mechanized formalizations compiling under Lake with zero sorries; interactive Jupyter reproduction notebooks; and deterministic deposit verification tooling.

Reproduction.

python -m pip install -e ".[dev]"
python verify_deposit.py --run-tests --lean

Epistemic Boundaries. The monograph investigates finite-dimensional quotient spaces of discrete cell complexes under exact arithmetic. It does not assert infinite-dimensional continuum Hodge theorems or dynamical quantum evolution. General finite-dimensional propositions have prose proofs and are classical background. Lean checks the conditional finite integer-list certificate and specified finite-model lemmas, without certificate existence or Python implementation correctness. The earlier general Aronsson assertion remains withdrawn.

Exact rational feasibility, stationarity, squared-norm and PSD checks; exact coherence when the required moduli are rational, binary64 diagnostics otherwise. The contribution is weighted graph quotient optimization presented through independently checkable exact certificates, a rational computational companion, and scoped finite Lean mechanization; bounded-circulation duality has the direct predecessor Jiang, Lim, Yao and Ye (2011), doi:10.1007/s10107-010-0419-x.
